question: Design a high-detail SOP to handle late-unit delivery for an angry customer while preserving trust and future referrals.
trainee_answer: I open with acknowledgement and ownership. I confirm the exact booking identifier, promised handover date, and present status from the logistics checkpoint. I explain the root cause in plain language and avoid defensive wording. I provide a revised ETA with a confidence level, then offer two practical alternatives: interim mobility support and accessory compensation aligned with policy. I set a communication cadence with explicit checkpoints and one accountable contact person. I escalate internally to sales supervisor and distribution PIC if timeline risk exceeds threshold. I document every agreement in CRM and repeat key points in writing to avoid ambiguity. I close by confirming customer priorities, inviting objections, and asking permission for proactive updates until handover is completed. After delivery, I conduct closure follow-up and collect feedback to prevent recurrence.

question: Create a manager-ready coaching answer for handling repeated post-service complaints with escalation and recovery actions.
trainee_answer: First, validate the customer experience and summarize all prior incidents to show continuity. Second, perform issue triage by severity, safety impact, and downtime impact. Third, assign one owner across departments and lock a target resolution window. Fourth, escalate to service manager with a written diagnostic summary and required approvals. Fifth, communicate status at fixed intervals even if no major update is available. Sixth, provide goodwill action according to branch policy when service delay crosses threshold. Seventh, verify fix effectiveness through a follow-up check and customer confirmation. Finally, run internal retrospective: root cause, process gap, owner, and prevention action with due date.

question: Provide a comprehensive answer for converting a hesitant test-drive customer into a committed next step without hard-selling.
trainee_answer: I begin by restating what the customer liked and what remains uncertain. I ask one clarifying question on budget comfort and one on family usage priority. I map those answers to variant value, ownership cost, and practical daily benefit instead of feature dumping. I handle objections with evidence and short comparisons, then give space for consideration. I propose one low-friction next commitment: booking review call, financing simulation, or accessory package confirmation. I summarize agreed points in a concise message and confirm the exact next contact time. I keep tone consultative and transparent, and avoid pressure language so trust remains intact.
